title: Trig graphs
examples: How does the period change when I multiply the x by two?
If the graph is shifted up by three, what does that mean?
What is the amplitude if the graph goes from minus five to five?

explain.say: Today we look at how to sketch trig graphs. We will look at period and amplitude first.
The period tells us how often the graph repeats its shape. For sine and cosine, the basic period is two pi.
If you have a graph like sine of x divided by three, the period stretches out. The new period becomes two pi times three.
The amplitude is the graph's maximum distance from the centre line. It is the coefficient in front of the trig function.
Let us look at a full transformation example. Consider the graph y equals two sine of x divided by four plus one.

faq.q: What does the amplitude mean on the graph?
faq.a: The amplitude is half the distance between the highest and lowest points. It shows how far the graph moves up or down from its middle line.
asks: What is the vertical stretch factor?
How do I find the height of the wave?

faq.q: If I see sin(2x), what is the period?
faq.a: The period is found by dividing two pi by the number multiplying x. So for two x, the period is two pi divided by two, which is pi.
asks: How does the period change if the number is bigger?
What is the period of sin(2x)?

faq.q: What is the effect of adding a number outside the function?
faq.a: Adding a number outside the function shifts the entire graph up or down. This is called a vertical shift.
asks: Does adding a number change the period?
What does the + three do to the graph?

faq.a: The amplitude is always a positive value. If you see a negative sign, it just reflects the graph across the horizontal line.
asks: What if the coefficient is negative?

faq.q: What is the general form for these graphs?
faq.a: The general form is y equals A times trig of (B x) plus C. A is amplitude, B affects the period, and C is the vertical shift.
asks: What are the parts of the equation?
What does the equation look like?

facts: The basic period for both sine and cosine graphs is two pi units.
The amplitude is determined by the coefficient multiplying the sine or cosine function.
A number inside the function affects the period by dividing two pi by that number.
A number added outside the function shifts the graph vertically up or down.

quiz.say: What is the amplitude of the graph y equals three cosine x?
quiz.why: The amplitude is the number directly in front of the cosine function, which is three.

wrong.0: This mistake forgets to look at the coefficient, assuming the base function has an amplitude of one.
wrong.1: This mistake might confuse amplitude with the vertical shift, which is zero here.
wrong.3: This mistake suggests the amplitude is the entire term, but amplitude is just the single multiplier.

quiz.say: What is the period of the graph y equals sin(x divided by five)?
quiz.why: The period is two pi divided by the number inside the bracket, which is five. So it is two pi divided by five.

wrong.0: This mistake treats the number inside the bracket as the period itself, rather than affecting it.
wrong.1: This mistake assumes the graph is unchanged and ignores the effect of the number inside the function.
wrong.3: This mistake incorrectly divides two pi by five, forgetting to multiply by two.

quiz.say: For y equals sin(x) plus two, what is the vertical shift?
quiz.why: The number added outside the function, two, moves the entire graph up by two units.

wrong.0: This mistake ignores the added constant, assuming the graph stays centered on the x-axis.
wrong.1: This mistake might incorrectly use the coefficient of x as the vertical shift.
wrong.3: This mistake confuses the vertical shift with the standard period of the sine function.
